rationale: Exclude (E01 - wrong topic). This study conducts an environmental-law and content analysis of 36 municipal tender specifications for commercial beach tourist concessions (Fiscal Tourist Units) in Mar del Plata, Argentina, focusing on coastal adaptation, aquifer protection, water-efficiency clauses, and Nature-Based Solutions. It does not examine household or community water or sanitation service access (fails Criterion 1) or any household/community water or sanitation access outcome (fails Criterion 4).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Both the narrow rule-type reading and the plain Criterion 2 reading yield exclusion because the study fails Criterion 1 (it examines coastal ecosystem governance and commercial beach tourist unit concessions rather than household or community water/sanitation service access) and Criterion 4 (outcomes concern inclusion of Nature-Based Solutions and environmental clauses in beach concession tenders rather than household/community service access).

evidence_quotes.quote: Nature-Based Solutions in Coastal Governance, A Legal Analysis of Beach Concession Contracts in Mar del Plata, Argentina
analyzes 36 tender specifications corresponding to the Fiscal Tourist Units managed by the Municipality.

The content analysis indicates that, although environmental management and water-efficiency requirements are increasingly incorporated into tender specifications, explicit NBS criteria remain largely absent.
